text:
Ravi S: hey all, day 1 question. i merged the onboarding kubeconfig and created a context alias `rdw-dev` to save typing. when i do `kubectl config use-context rdw-dev` it switches but `kubectl get pods -n rl-ml` fails with Forbidden and mentions `system:serviceaccount:default:ravi-sa`. why is my context pointing at a SA?
Ben (DevEx): welcome Ravi! aliases can be tricky if you created the context by copying an existing one that referenced a service account user. what command did you use to create the alias?
Ravi S: i did `kubectl config rename-context redwood-dev rdw-dev` after merging configs. i figured rename would be safe.
Ben (DevEx): rename should preserve the context's user binding. if the original context referenced a serviceaccount user, renaming won't switch it to your Okta user. run `kubectl config view -o jsonpath='{.contexts[?(@.name=="rdw-dev")].context.user}'` to see which user is attached.
Ravi S: that returns `system:serviceaccount:default:ravi-sa`. oh shoot. how do i switch it back to my okta user?
Marta I: you can `kubectl config set-context rdw-dev --user=ravi@example.com`. also double-check `kubectl config get-contexts rdw-dev` to confirm.
Ravi S: tried that; now `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n rl-ml` returns `no` (user not in team). i assume that's expected since i'm new?
Ben (DevEx): yep, that's expected. two things: (1) the 401 vs 403 difference — if you see Unauthorized (401) first, that usually means the auth exec token is stale or missing; (2) 403 means auth worked but RBAC denies you. since you're seeing `no` on can-i, it's RBAC. request a personal namespace or wait for identity sync.
Ravi S: ok. is there a safe way to create a dev namespace myself? or do i need infra?
Marta I: infra-provisioned personal namespaces are the norm so we can track ownership and quotas. ping infra in this thread and they'll create `dev-ravi`. Sam usually does them.
Ravi S: ping infra? @infra-bot, can we get a dev namespace for ravi?
infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-6122 to create namespace `dev-ravi` and bind `edit` to system:serviceaccount:default:ravi-sa (priority: normal).
Ravi S: thanks! while we wait, any tips to avoid this for others merging kubeconfigs?
Ben (DevEx): a few tips: (1) avoid blindly copying contexts; use `kubectl config use-context` to switch rather than renaming if unsure, (2) when merging use `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:~/.kube/onboard kubectl config view --merge --flatten > /tmp/merged && mv /tmp/merged ~/.kube/config` to avoid duplicate user blocks, (3) run `kubectl config get-contexts` and look at the USER column to ensure it points to your email user, not a SA, (4) if you see 401, clear `~/.kube/cache` and re-run the exec login.
Ravi S: infra-bot updated: INFRA-6122 completed, `dev-ravi` created. `kubectl auth can-i create deployments -n dev-ravi` -> yes. deploying sample now.
Marta I: nice. one more thing: if you want a shorthand for the context without touching the original, create a new context pointing to the same cluster but explicitly set the user: `kubectl config set-context rdw-dev-user --cluster=<cluster-name> --user=ravi@example.com --namespace=dev-ravi`. that way the alias is explicit and safe.
Ravi S: will do, thanks for the help — saved me from accidentally using a CI SA. :raised_hands:
